mcqs.question: In R. Rajagopal v. State of Tamil Nadu (1994), what aspect of personality rights was recognised under Article 21?
options: The right to control one’s identity
The right to commercialise every public office
The right to impose criminal defamation
The right to obtain a government domicile certificate
mcqs.explanation: R. Rajagopal v. State of Tamil Nadu (1994) recognised the right to control one’s identity under Article 21. The case did not concern criminal defamation or domicile certification.

mcqs.question:
Match the cases concerning personality-rights protection with their holdings:

List-I
(a) Rajinikanth case
(b) DM Entertainment v. Baby Gift House
(c) Anil Kapoor case
(d) Jackie Shroff case

List-II
(i) Protection of “jhakaas”
(ii) Restraint on Daler Mehndi dolls
(iii) Restraint on “Main Hoon Rajnikanth”
(iv) Protection concerning e-commerce and AI chatbots

Select the correct code:
options: a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv
a-ii, b-iii, c-iv, d-i
a-i, b-iv, c-ii, d-iii
a-iv, b-i, c-iii, d-ii
mcqs.explanation: The correct pairs are Rajinikanth—“Main Hoon Rajnikanth”, DM Entertainment—Daler Mehndi dolls, Anil Kapoor—“jhakaas”, and Jackie Shroff—e-commerce and AI chatbots. The other codes interchange the holdings among these cases.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements:
Statement A: In the Arijit Singh case, the Bombay High Court permitted AI voice cloning.
Statement B: In Digital Collectibles v. Galactus Funware, rights were expanded at the cost of free speech.
options: Both Statement A and Statement B are true
Both Statement A and Statement B are false
Statement A is true, Statement B is false
Statement A is false, Statement B is true
mcqs.explanation: Both statements are false. AI voice cloning was restrained in the Arijit Singh case, while Digital Collectibles v. Galactus Funware refused to expand rights at the cost of free speech.

mcqs.question: In which year did the United Nations declare internet access to be a human right?
mcqs.explanation: The United Nations declared internet access a human right in 2016. The years 2019 and 2020 relate to Indian judicial recognition discussed in other cases, while 2025 is not the year of the UN declaration.

mcqs.question:
Consider the following statements regarding BharatNet and digital literacy:

1. BharatNet targeted 6.5 lakh villages.
2. By January 2025, 1.99 lakh villages, or 30.4%, were connected under BharatNet.
3. NASSCOM reported in 2023 that only 37% of Indians were digitally literate.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
options: 1 and 2 only
2 only
1 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
mcqs.explanation: All three statements are correct. BharatNet’s target was 6.5 lakh villages, 1.99 lakh villages were connected by January 2025, and NASSCOM reported digital literacy among only 37% of Indians in 2023.

mcqs.question: Which one of the following statements regarding criminal defamation in India is incorrect?
options: Sections 499 and 500 of the IPC provide for up to 2 years of imprisonment, fine or both.
Sections 499 and 500 of the IPC provide for up to 3 years of imprisonment, fine or both.
The punishment may include imprisonment and fine.
Criminal defamation is dealt with under Sections 499 and 500 of the IPC.
mcqs.explanation: The incorrect statement is the one mentioning 3 years. Sections 499 and 500 of the IPC provide for up to 2 years of imprisonment, fine or both.

mcqs.question: What was the holding of the Supreme Court in Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016)?
options: It upheld criminal defamation, holding reputation to be part of Article 21.
It abolished criminal defamation, holding reputation outside Article 21.
It upheld criminal defamation only under Article 19 and not Article 21.
It transferred criminal defamation entirely to the jurisdiction of State legislatures.
mcqs.explanation: In Subramanian Swamy v. Union of India (2016), the Supreme Court upheld criminal defamation and held that reputation is part of Article 21. The judgment therefore did not abolish criminal defamation or exclude Article 21.

mcqs.question: Why did Ho adivasis protest in West Singhbhum on 9 September 2025?
options: They protested against DC Chandan Kumar for allegedly removing Mundas.
They protested against the Supreme Court for abolishing the Manki-Munda system.
They protested against the United Nations for declaring internet access a human right.
They protested against the State of Bihar over the Daler Mehndi dolls case.
mcqs.explanation: Ho adivasis protested in West Singhbhum against DC Chandan Kumar for allegedly removing Mundas. The protest concerned the local Manki-Munda system and not the unrelated judicial or international matters in the other options.

mcqs.keyword: Historical demographic change and customary governance
mcqs.question:
Assertion (A): The number of Dikkus in Kolhan increased from 1,579 in 1867 to 15,755 in 1897.
Reason (R): Mora Ho v. State of Bihar held that Wilkinson’s Rules were formal law.
options: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true, but R is NOT the correct explanation of A
A is true, but R is false
A is false, but R is true
mcqs.explanation: Assertion A is true: Dikkus increased from 1,579 in 1867 to 15,755 in 1897. Reason R is false because Mora Ho v. State of Bihar held that Wilkinson’s Rules were customs, not formal law.

mcqs.question: Which of the following was cited as an example in the discussion of provincial citizenship and domicile politics?
options: Jharkhand’s domicile policy and the post-2019 domicile rules in Jammu and Kashmir
Kerala’s domicile policy and the post-2016 domicile rules in Tamil Nadu
Manipur’s domicile policy and the post-2020 domicile rules in West Bengal
Bihar’s domicile policy and the post-2015 domicile rules in Odisha
mcqs.explanation: The examples cited were Jharkhand, formed in 2000, and Jammu and Kashmir’s domicile rules after 2019. The other combinations are not the examples identified in this context.

mcqs.question: Which set of constitutional provisions was linked with the discussion of provincial citizenship and domicile politics?
options: Articles 15, 16, 16(2) and 19
Articles 14, 21, 32 and 356
Articles 17, 18, 20 and 22
Articles 29, 30, 44 and 51A
mcqs.explanation: The relevant provisions are Articles 15, 16, 16(2) and 19. The other options substitute provisions that were not identified in this discussion.
